<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/state-machine.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 819c0679a8917fddd8dba7314c8de2c27d03e46b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `22aa5b787038000ab4e400755e9a4090de90510e` — the merge of head `c147762a1c45aa8d7b742c34f838d6d723d6de75` into base `819c0679a8917fddd8dba7314c8de2c27d03e46b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 22aa5b787038000ab4e400755e9a4090de90510e && git checkout 22aa5b787038000ab4e400755e9a4090de90510e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 819c0679a8917fddd8dba7314c8de2c27d03e46b c147762a1c45aa8d7b742c34f838d6d723d6de75 && git checkout -B drift-repro 819c0679a8917fddd8dba7314c8de2c27d03e46b && git merge --no-ff c147762a1c45aa8d7b742c34f838d6d723d6de75

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 819c0679a8917fddd8dba7314c8de2c27d03e46b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 819c0679a8917fddd8dba7314c8de2c27d03e46b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：初始化数据里，如果某条记录的"唯一标识字段"留空，现在加载时会拒收这条记录，并说明是哪个对象、第几条、缺哪个字段、怎么改；其它记录照常加载，系统照常启动。
- 为什么做：以前这种记录每次重启、安装或发布都会被再插入一遍，数据越积越多重复，且没有任何提示。
- 出错会怎样：已有的重复数据不会被自动清理；作者需要给记录补上该字段的值。
- 要你做什么：无（这是你选的方案 B1）。区域补一张文档跟进卡后，交席位做合同复审。

## 席位核对

**L1-a: ACCEPT with one required item before landing** · head `acdab3018ae0ad4de711fa93a7bb3cf8fe52fb6c` · Fixes #34857 #35336 (#35376 rides) · 2026-11-19T11:16Z

Readings: K=10 (no main merge owed); `check-governed-merges --pr 35459` not governed (0 of 13 paths), 607 changed lines; `merge-tree` against main clean; CI 60 success / 10 skipped / 0 failed.

**Code: sound, and it is the ruling.** The maintainer chose B1 on the seat's decision card (seat ruling record 7000515976), extended to single-field keys on #35336.
- One blank rule, `isBlankSeedKeyValue` (no value, `null`, `''`, no trim), now shared by `seedLandedKey`, `externalIdKey` and the new refusal.
- The refusal sits in the record loop only under `keyedMode`, after expressions resolve and before references resolve, so a deferred reference still holds its authored value and is not blank (pinned in `seed-loader-deferred-key-reference.test.ts`).
- Each refused record is an error in the result and `continue`s, so the boot never fails. The `error` log fires once per dataset and is suppressed on `dryRun`, while the dry run still reports the error.
- The #28952 dataset-level `warn` is removed rather than doubled, as A2 chose, and pinned (`logger.warn` not called).
- #35376 is wording only: the duplicate-fallback refusal and its docblock drop the upgrade-within-process cause. What is refused is unchanged.

**Evidence.** A1 measured 2, 3, 4 rows over three loads before the fix and 1, 1, 1 after, on single-field, default-`name`, composite `''` and composite `null` keys. The dogfood battery ran on this exact head (7007256277) with 4092 tests passing and zero blank-key refusals in the boot logs, so no shipped seed trips the new refusal.

**Declaration: agreed.** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` / `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` / `minor` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`. It carries a BREAKING banner, the FROM / TO lines and the author's one-line fix, and exactly one marker, `registered seed-key-blank-record-refused`, with its D3 entry at `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.seed-key-blank-record-refused.ts`. The report shows `check-adr-0087-registration` exit 0, with no id collision against main's `18.seed-object-unknown-refused`.

**R1 (required before landing): `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` → `#N`.** L1 checklist line 18 says to file the card and write its number in place of `owed`. The changeset already names the three anchors (`skills/objectstack-data/references/seeds.md` :48, :68, :93), so file the card from them and change the line in the changeset and the PR body. A push that only applies R1 needs no fresh L1.

**Routing: L2 owed.** There are two contract faces: the narrowing declaration, and the non-test `packages/spec/src/**` path (the D3 entry). Seat 5 runs the L2. pkg-1 lands after it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d56b6f80c17b62bb829152d0b176cceea06b61bd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.seed-key-blank-record-refused.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader-empty-key-warn.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader-deferred-key-reference.test.ts, content/docs/data-modeling/seed-data.mdx (read for agreement)

### ① Derived judgments

PR #35459, cards #34857 and #35336 (#35376 rides). Read: both cards with every comment (rulings 7000515976 and 7000600379, the claim and its two amendments, both os-dev-reports), the PR body, the file list (13 files), the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs. The head moved during this review from `acdab301` to `d56b6f80`: the one commit between them changes one line of `.changeset/34857-seed-blank-key-record-refused.md` (`Skills-docs: follow-up owed` became `Skills-docs: follow-up #35480`), and the PR body carries the same line. Card #35480 is open, `domain:skills`, and names `skills/objectstack-data/references/seeds.md` with the three anchors. No code, test, doc or ledger byte differs between the two heads, so every code judgment below was formed on `acdab301` and holds on `d56b6f80`.

- **Accept set, keyed modes (`ignore`, `upsert`, `update`): a record with a blank key field is refused.** Blank is no value, `null` or `''`, in any component of a composite `externalId` or in the one field of a single-field key. Right: it is ruling B1 (7000515976) as extended to single-field keys (7000600379). One helper, `isBlankSeedKeyValue`, now serves the refusal, `seedLandedKey` and the composite arm of `externalIdKey`.
- **A dataset whose every record keys empty stops loading entirely.** The dataset-level `warn` is gone and each record is refused. This is the widest consequence of the change: a dataset left on the default key `name` over records that carry no `name` used to seed (and duplicate on a persistent database); it now seeds nothing and reports each record. Right: the rule admits no carve-out for "all of them", the claim left this choice to the dev (kept or folded), and the changeset states it. In-repo stock is 0 of 26 datasets.
- **`update` mode: a silent skip becomes a reported error**, and the load's `success` turns false. Right, and declared.
- **A key field whose expression evaluates empty is refused** (`os.user.id` with no identity). Right: the check sits after `resolveSeedRecord` and before reference resolution, as the ruling's execution text places it; such a record keyed `''` and re-inserted before. The changeset and the ledger entry say "after expressions resolve"; the docs page does not (N2).
- **A key reference that is authored and resolves empty is NOT refused.** Right, and pinned as a CONTROL in both `ignore` and `upsert` (three loads, one row), beside a record whose key reference is authored `''` and is refused.
- **A whitespace-only value is a value** (no trim). Unchanged, pinned as a CONTROL.
- **A mode-less load (no `mode`, no `defaultMode`) is not keyed and is unchanged.** Right as stated; only a request built without the parse reaches it.
- **Dry run (`validate`) reports the refusal and logs nothing.** Right, pinned.
- **Public surface: no schema, export or Zod change.** The load result gains `ReferenceResolutionError` rows with `targetField: '(externalId)'`, and `success` is false where it was true. Read at every consumer: the boot seed (AppPlugin) reports and continues; the marketplace install reports counts; the publish receipt carries `seedApplied.success: false`. No in-repo caller sets `haltOnError`, whose default is `false`, so "every other record and dataset loads" holds on every shipped path.
- **Against the published spec on `main`:** `SeedSchema.mode` declares "Every mode matches on `externalId`, so a replay finds the row an earlier load wrote instead of inserting it again". A blank-key record defeated that sentence. The narrowing makes the spec's own promise real; it takes no declared capability away. ADR-0038 reads the same way (seeds are upserts keyed on `externalId`), and no ADR decides the opposite.
- **`findDuplicateFallbackSets`: wording only.** What is refused is unchanged. The cause it drops is gone on this tree: `8596c80eda` (an upgrade replaces the package's datasets on the replay list) is an ancestor of the head.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor`, with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on the PR body and in the changeset body. Correct.

- `narrowed` is the right kind: a value an author could write is now refused. A kind takes at least `minor` on a package whose published source the diff moves, and `seed-loader.ts` is that source. `patch` would be wrong here and the level gate would refuse it.
- `minor`, not `major`: the launch-window rule (ADR-0087, the level half) ships a metadata-facing break as `minor` and makes the banner and the disposition the carriers. Both are present: the `!` title, the `**BREAKING**` paragraph with FROM, TO and the author's fix, and the adr-0087 marker reading `registered seed-key-blank-record-refused`, an id that resolves and is new in this diff.
- `no-migration-prescription` is closed to a `narrowed` changeset (ADR-0087, the disposition-vocabulary addendum as amended), so a registered semantic entry is the required disposition, and it is the one taken.
- `@objectstack/spec` is not named in the changeset although the ledger entry lives in its source. Accepted: the fixed group versions in lockstep, the level predicate asks for at least one moved package at `minor`, and the sibling entry `18.seed-object-unknown-refused` landed the same way.
- `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on `d56b6f80`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`:** empty in both os-dev-reports. Nothing to answer.
- **Dev deviations, each answered.** The `packages/spec` fence: one data-only ledger entry, authorized by the claim amendment 7003089279. The widened test surface (objectql, runtime and three metadata-protocol harness files): covered by the claim amendment 7006195595. The #35376 docs bullet: inside the claimed surface. The stray `/final.pid` at the filesystem root: outside the repository and outside this review; a person removes it.
- **Out-of-scope findings.** The Skills-docs follow-up is now card #35480 (L1's R1, confirmed above). The stale comment in `seed-loader-locale-scope.test.ts` is noted in the PR and accepted as a note.
- **SQL push-down:** no finding. The change adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. The refusal reads the in-memory record before any lookup, and the dataset-level scan it removes was in memory too.
- **Dogfood battery (required by the `(narrowing)` arm): MISSING on this head.** The newest os-dev-report (7007256277) pins it to `acdab3018ae0ad4de711fa93a7bb3cf8fe52fb6c`: lock verdict `command-exit 0`, 482 files and 4092 tests passed, zero blank-key refusals in the boot logs. `d56b6f80` is a non-merge commit on top of that sha. The land gate accepts the head itself or a sha the head reaches over merges of the base alone, so it will refuse this pin. The battery must be re-run and reported on the final head before landing. S1 below moves the head again, so one run on the head that carries its fix covers both.
- **Check-runs.** On `acdab301` all 70 concluded: `success`, or `skipped` by the pull-request speed (the dogfood shards among them), including every required context. On `d56b6f80` the runs had not all concluded when this record was written: `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` and the PR-body guards were `success`; the build, type-check and test shards were still running. This record certifies none of those; the landing seat reads them.
- **Noted for the seat, not graded.** No authoring door judges this rule: `defineSeed`, `os validate` and lint read no record key value, so a code-defined stack first meets the refusal at boot. The ruling scoped the refusal to the load, so this is not a defect of the PR; it is a candidate follow-up card under Prime Directive 12 (reject at authoring).

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.seed-key-blank-record-refused.ts` (hits).** Holds.

- Shape: `id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`, typed `SemanticMigration`; the filename is derived from the id and the major; no id collides (main's `18.seed-object-unknown-refused` is distinct). `conversionIds` is rightly absent: there is no mechanical rewrite, since only the author knows the value that names the row. `relevantWhen` is rightly absent: the surface also lives in stored `seed` items and package bodies, which no top-level stack key proves absent, so the entry stays listed.
- D3 ("never silence"): the entry names the judgment delegated to the consumer and how to prove it (every record carries each key field; three restarts hold one row per record; no blank-key refusal in the boot log or the load result). The criteria are checkable by a consumer's own verify loop.
- Against the code, sentence by sentence: the three keyed modes, the three blank spellings, composite and single-field (default `name`), "one error naming the object, the record index, the blank field and the fix", "once per dataset" in the log, "after expressions resolve and before references do", and "rows earlier loads duplicated are left" all match `loadDataset` at `seed-loader.ts:2330-2359`. The measured 2, 3, 4 is the cards' own reading.
- No tracker number in any printed string; the two card numbers sit in the leading comment, as the sibling entries do.

**`packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts` (implementing).** The refusal agrees with the ruling and the entry: placed after expression resolution, the organization stamp and the per-organization id, before any reference resolves; `errored` counts it so the four counters still reconcile against `total`; nothing of the record is written or deferred; the log line is said once per dataset and never on a dry run. I tried to break it on a composite key containing the stamped organization column (stamped before the check, so not blank), on an `id` key under per-organization replay (the assigned id is on the record by then), on a deferred key reference (authored, so not blank) and on `haltOnError` (off on every shipped path). It held.

S1 (should-fix) — the default-key wording never prints on a shipped path, and its pin exercises a path production does not take. `blankSeedKeyRefusal` adds "(the default key when a dataset names none)" when `dataset.externalId === undefined` (`seed-loader.ts:2344`, `:489`). Every production caller parses its request through `SeedLoaderRequestSchema` first (the boot seed, the per-organization replay and the install through `loadStored`; both publish doors through `safeParse`; this file's own comment at `:312-314` says so), and `SeedSchema.externalId` carries `.default('name')` (`seed.zod.ts:212`). A parsed dataset therefore always carries `externalId: 'name'`, the branch is false, and the author who never wrote `externalId` is told only that the record "is keyed on externalId 'name'", a key they never wrote. That is the commonest way to meet this refusal, and the one where a whole dataset stops seeding. The pin at `seed-loader-empty-key-warn.test.ts:177-186` passes because it hands `load()` an unparsed literal. The PR body's "default `name` (message says it is the default)" is thus true only for a direct, unparsed caller. Fix: decide the wording from something that survives the parse (for a single-field key of `name`, say that `name` is also the key a dataset gets when it names none), or drop the hint and the claim; and pin the message through a parsed request (`loadStored`, or `SeedLoaderRequestSchema.parse`). The refusal itself is correct on every path; this is the prescription's text and its test.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract; ride the S1 push or a follow-up):

- N1 (nit) — `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:9080-9082`, outside the diff, still says "The boot loader never refuses; it warns once for a keyed dataset whose every record keys empty". This PR makes both halves false. It is the only such sentence left in source or hand-written docs.
- N2 (nit) — `content/docs/data-modeling/seed-data.mdx:83` says the check "reads the key as written in the seed". An expression in a key field is evaluated first and is refused when it comes out empty, and the same page says at `:782` that a record with `os.user.id` "still seeds". One clause closes it: the key is read after the record's expressions resolve.
- N3 (nit) — the docblock calls `isBlankSeedKeyValue` "the one blank rule" `externalIdKey` keys `''` by. The single-field arm is `String(record[externalId] ?? '')`, which is also `''` for an empty array, so a single-field key authored `[]` still keys empty, is not refused and is inserted on every load. Not reachable from any stock dataset; a follow-up card, or one line in the helper.

**The two pin files (enforcing).** They pin the composite key with `''`, `null` and an omitted component (three loads, 2, 2, 2 rows, one error and one log line per load), the single-field key, an expression that evaluates empty, `update`, the dry run, the all-empty dataset (every record refused, one line, no `warn`), and the CONTROLs: a fully keyed dataset, a whitespace-only value, a deferred key reference in `ignore` and `upsert`. The dev's ablation (the blank filter forced empty: 11 refusal pins red, every CONTROL green) shows the pins bite. The one gap is S1's: the default-key message is pinned on the unparsed path only.

**`content/docs/data-modeling/seed-data.mdx` (read for agreement).** Import Modes and the composite-key section state the rule as the loader enforces it; every `defineSeed` example on the page carries its key field (the `TestUser` example now names `externalId: 'email'`); the fallback bullet matches the new refusal text. N2 is the one imprecision.

One should-fix (S1), three nits; a delta review is owed on the S1 fix, and the dogfood battery on the head that carries it.

Security-touching: no

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-34857-blank-seed-key-refused`
Reviewed-by: `isolated-l2-35459`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8aa97502e42b6f561a89cfedfc6a74a9b63bd2f9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.seed-key-blank-record-refused.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader-empty-key-warn.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, content/docs/data-modeling/seed-data.mdx (read for agreement)

### ① Derived judgments

Delta review of PR #35459 (cards #34857 and #35336) against the record on `d56b6f80c17b62bb829152d0b176cceea06b61bd`. The head is one plain commit on top of it, four files, 42 lines added and 13 removed; the base is unchanged. Read: that commit's diff, the tree at the head where it lands, the card's newest os-dev-report (7008747872), card #35485, and the check-runs on the head. Everything the first record judged outside these four files is byte-identical and stands as judged.

- **Accept set: unchanged.** The commit moves no refusal. What a keyed load refuses, what it writes and what it counts are the same lines as on the reviewed head; only the wording of one refusal message changes.
- **Refusal text, one clause.** A record refused on a single-field key of `name` now reads "keyed on externalId 'name' (also the key a dataset gets when it names none)". Every other key, a composite containing `name` included, carries no such clause. Right: the sentence is true whether the author wrote `externalId: 'name'` or left it out, so it cannot mislead either reader.
- **No schema, export, ledger or changeset byte moves.** The ledger entry and the changeset are those of the reviewed head.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still correct: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, the BREAKING paragraph and the `registered seed-key-blank-record-refused` marker.
